main_text.p: consistat Ant. I. 17. 10 Herodem sub [illegible, ~10 letters] finem vel ruentum suum mutasse, atque Herodes [illegible, ~6 letters] (quem prioribus tabulis regni successorem designarat) Galilææ & Peræ Tetrarchiam constituit. Regnum vero Archelao legitimo fuisse. His igitur ex parentis testamento Rex confirmatus, [illegible, ~8 letters] Herodes obierat, Regno igitur [?] quoniam [illegible, ~6 letters] Regis morte [illegible, ~5 letters] nisi fama de Herodis morte, & [illegible, ~8 letters] tum vulgatum. Hunc Ihesus, [illegible, ~12 letters] gressus, regem creatum audit, [illegible, ~8 letters] trā Iudææ concedit, atque in Galilæam [illegible, ~6 letters] ex testamento factus erat [?] laetus) ducem [illegible, ~5 letters] petit. Hanc ante Iesu in Nazareth prius quam initium [illegible, ~8 letters] cum initio regni Archelai [illegible, ~10 letters] consequente [illegible, ~5 letters] & quoniam hic fuit terminus itineris [illegible, ~6 letters] pto, ut Nazarethum abierint, ibique primum [illegible, ~4 letters] collocaverint, necesse est, ut reliqui Ipsius [illegible, ~7 letters] fuerit ille ipse dies, quo Ihesus a [illegible, ~5 letters] discessit; ut dies itineris absolvit, quo Nazarethum [illegible, ~5 letters] gressus, non plus abierat a primo [illegible, ~4 letters] dir, quam iuncris ultimus à primo.

§ 3 His characteribus ita perpensis, per omnia prohibemur cum illa tenere, qui maxime Cartei post anni Iul. XXII dicti Novembris sive collocandum statuunt, qui tamen plurimorum error est, nulla re passandis, quaque tot viros doctos eaecat. Hoc tempora everterc non tantum, sed & nationem turbare. Omnes fere ignoscunt quam vulgarum, non aberrare: aut qui id monstrat non affligunt, [illegible, ~6 letters] quot oculos, effectum revera Christum post Herodis mortem & initium regiminis Archelai demum quanto [illegible, ~4 letters] fuit.

page.notes: Most of the page is blurred and faded, and many words could not be read with certainty. Those passages are marked [illegible] or [?] and are not reconstructed. The Greek and Hebrew names and the reference "Ant. I. 17. 10" are as far as they can be made out. The text printed in the right margin belongs to the neighbouring page and is left out. The final line near the lower right may be a catchword, but it is not clear enough to read.
